correctness.rationale: A nonselected cell has exactly row-plus-column selected rook neighbors. Every incidence cycle edge set is itself a fort; a minimal fort containing a cycle must equal that cycle. Square spanning cycles contain a proper perfect-matching fort. An acyclic incidence forest has at most m+n-2 edges unless it is a spanning tree; the latter has an internal edge removable while retaining all positive row/column degrees, producing a smaller fort. Cross supports give minimal forts of size m+n-2; nonspanning even cycles give minimal forts of size m+n-1 when the dimensions differ by one. Exact-original-adjacency exhaustive dynamic programming verifies all proper subforts across ten boards (1,414,992 masks), not just single deletions. All statements assume m,n>=2; finite checks do not constitute infinite proof.

value.rationale: The minimal-fort hypergraph is the exact obstruction system to zero forcing. Its rank is a natural extremal structural invariant not determined by smallest fort size, fort packing or number of minimal forts. The formula is uniform across an infinite graph family and exhibits a sharp, structurally explained extra edge precisely for consecutive rectangle sides. The proof identifies cycle-versus-forest mechanisms and constructs extremal obstructions, useful for maximal failed-forcing-set and hypergraph rank questions.
